name: Two Euclidean pulse generators per track combined with Boolean logic (OR, XOR, AND, SUB), per-generator rotation and whole-track rotation, then printed to an ordinary step sequence for hand edits; also used to redistribute an existing bassline and to leave gaps an arpeggiator fills
goal: Generate musically coherent, non-obvious drum and melodic patterns by combining two Euclidean pulse generators on one track. Each generator spreads N pulses as evenly as possible over the track length (e.g. 16 or 32 steps); numbers that do not divide the length (5, 9, 11, 12) give the interesting grooves. Combine the two with a Boolean operator: OR (any pulse plays; overlaps become one note), XOR (overlaps are removed, leaving space), AND (only overlaps play; the number of possible notes is limited by the smaller pulse count) or SUB (generator 1 minus where it overlaps generator 2, a way to carve notes out). Rotate each generator to change their relationship, then rotate the whole track to move the downbeat of the combined pattern. Print the result to a normal step sequence to edit single notes, apply the same Euclidean distribution to a pre-programmed melodic line (notes stay, positions change), randomise the Euclidean settings with a snapshot to return to, and let an arpeggiator with step offsets fill the gaps. Delta beyond our probability/seeded loop skills: the two-generator Boolean combine plus print-to-steps workflow, mapped to Polyrhythm Studio lanes.

source.title: How I Actually Use Euclidean Sequencing on Digitone 2
source.transcript_note: Hardware walkthrough; device button combos and part-two teaser dropped.

prerequisites: Step sequencer or DAW/MIDI tool that can compute Euclidean patterns, or Web Audio / JS: compute Bjorklund patterns for two (pulses, length, rotation) sets and combine the boolean arrays per step (implementation note)
Drum and bass voices; optional arpeggiator

inputs.name: length
inputs.description: Track length in steps (16 or 32 in the video)

inputs.name: track_rotation
inputs.description: Rotation applied to the combined pattern

outputs.name: pattern
outputs.description: Combined boolean step pattern per track

outputs.name: printed_sequence
outputs.description: Ordinary step sequence after printing, ready for hand edits

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
AND with no overlaps is silent; raise pulse counts or rotate until hits appear.
Printing converts the pattern to fixed steps; Euclidean edits after that no longer apply unless you re-enable it.
Device button combos are product-specific and omitted; use any Euclidean tool. No numbers beyond pulses, length and rotations were given.

steps.action: Turn on Euclidean mode for a drum track. Set generator 1 to a simple count (e.g. 4 pulses over 16 steps) and listen; then try counts that do not divide 16 (5, 11).
steps.expect: Evenly spread hits; odd counts give syncopated grooves

steps.action: Enable generator 2 with a different count (e.g. 5 against 4) using OR. Rotate generator 2 to move its hits against generator 1.
steps.expect: An overlaid polyrhythmic feel that changes with rotation; overlaps count as one note

steps.action: Switch the operator: XOR to remove overlapping hits and open space; AND to keep only overlaps (raise counts, e.g. 9 and 12, and rotate until notes appear); SUB to keep generator 1 except where generator 2 lands.
steps.expect: Same two generators give four different densities and feels

steps.action: When an emergent pattern makes a new downbeat, use whole-track rotation (e.g. +3 steps) to move both generators together so that hit becomes step 1.
steps.expect: The pattern starts where you want without changing the inner relationship

steps.action: Print the pattern to the normal step sequencer, then hand-edit (move a note, leave room for a snare). Build hats on another track at length 32 with SUB to carve notes out of a dense generator 1.
steps.expect: Fixed, editable steps keep the Euclidean groove

steps.action: On a melodic (bass) track with notes already programmed, enable Euclidean mode so those notes are redistributed by the pulse pattern; add generator 2 with XOR and rotate the track. Randomise the Euclidean settings repeatedly until a version works.
steps.expect: Same notes in new rhythmic positions

steps.action: For sparse patterns, enable an arpeggiator and remove one arp note with its offset/step mask so it fills gaps without crowding.
steps.expect: Gaps filled with a grooving arp line

steps.action: For performance, change rotations and pulses on all tracks at once, and keep a snapshot so you can jump back to the original pattern.
steps.expect: Patterns tangle and untangle; one action returns to the saved state

verification: For pulses 4 and 5 over 16 steps, OR yields more hits than XOR, and AND yields only the shared positions.
Changing rotation of one generator changes the combined pattern while total pulse counts stay the same.
After printing, editing one step changes only that step.
The redistributed bassline keeps its original pitches.
